ai-at-work.title: OpenAI adds a prominent AI doomer to its board of directors
ai-at-work.excerpt: Paul Christiano, an influential AI researcher focused on alignment, is joining the OpenAI Foundation as a member of its board.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: OpenAI just hired Paul Christiano, a serious AI safety researcher, to sit on its foundation board. This matters because it signals that even the companies most enthusiastically shipping AI products are starting to genuinely engage with people asking "but should we though?" For those of us trying to figure out what AI tools to actually recommend to clients, having a vocal skeptic in the room at OpenAI is either encouraging or the world's most expensive PR move. Probably both.

ai-at-work.title: Apple Watch’s new AI features are normalizing the idea that technology is always listening
ai-at-work.excerpt: Apple says its new watches won’t save raw audio, but features that can transcribe recent speech and summarize ambient conversations raise new questions about consent, privacy, and how people behave wh
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Apple's latest Watch features can transcribe and summarize what you've said recently without storing the raw audio, but the distinction feels academic when the device is actively listening to your conversations anyway. For digital workplace folks, this matters because the same "we're not saving it" logic will inevitably show up in your company's monitoring tools, and employees will rightfully wonder what "not saving" actually means in practice. After three decades watching this stuff, I can tell you that normalizing surveillance by degrees is how you end up with a workforce that assumes everything they do is being watched, which is great for compliance and terrible for actual trust.

ai-at-work.title: Everything Apple announced at its fall iPhone event, from the foldable iPhone Duo to an always-listening Apple Watch
ai-at-work.excerpt: The main event was the tech giant's highly anticipated first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Apple finally shipped a foldable iPhone called the iPhone Duo, along with new Apple Watch features that listen to you constantly. For digital workplace folks, this matters because foldable phones change how we think about mobile work, screen real estate, and honestly, whether your VPN client can handle a folding display without having a nervous breakdown. Look, I've seen enough "revolutionary" device announcements to know that foldables are still solving a problem most office workers don't actually have, but hey, at least IT departments will finally have something genuinely new to worry about.

ai-at-work.title: Superintelligence is coming. Should we let it?
ai-at-work.excerpt: AI companies have been talking about superintelligent AI like it’s inevitable, but recent safety incidents like OpenAI’s Hugging Face breach are demonstrating the potential dangers of deploying AI sys
ai-at-work.dwp_take: AI companies are treating superintelligence like it's just around the corner while simultaneously proving they can't even secure the systems they have today. For digital workplace leaders, this matters because you're already being pressured to deploy AI tools into your environment, and security incidents should make you very skeptical about rushing adoption of any system you can't control or audit. Here's my take after three decades in this space: if your vendor can't tell you exactly how their AI makes decisions and where your data goes, you shouldn't let it anywhere near your workplace, superintelligent or not.

tools-tech.title: Anthropic maps three AI futures for 2030; the most extreme could upend the economy
tools-tech.excerpt: AI is evolving faster than most people, even those building it, could even fathom, and its impact on the workforce and the economy is, at this point, really anyone’s guess. Researchers from The Anthro
tools-tech.dwp_take: Anthropic released a framework mapping three possible AI scenarios through 2030, ranging from modest to economy-disrupting outcomes. Digital workplace leaders need to stop pretending they know which scenario will play out and start building resilience into their talent strategies instead. Here's the truth: the researchers themselves admit this is a guess, which means your five-year workforce plan built on certainty is already obsolete.

tools-tech.title: Layoff remorse: Gartner says at least one in three positions eliminated by AI will be restored by 2029–at a higher cost
tools-tech.excerpt: Gartner on Wednesday said that it expects 30% of the positions eliminated by AI-related layoffs to be refilled by 2029, suggesting that the initial terminations were ill-advised and excessive. “When b
tools-tech.dwp_take: Gartner is predicting that one in three jobs eliminated by AI layoffs will come back by 2029, basically admitting the cuts were premature and too aggressive. This matters because it validates what workplace leaders should already know: automation should augment your workforce, not replace it wholesale. The real kicker is those rehired positions will cost more to fill, which means companies just paid to learn an expensive lesson about acting on hype instead of strategy.

tools-tech.title: Adobe Acrobat evolves beyond PDFs with enterprise search, AI content creation
tools-tech.excerpt: Adobe on Wednesday unveiled a range of updates to Acrobat, including the ability to turn PDF documents into interactive visual reports and podcasts. And a new Knowledge Base feature connects Adobe’s A
tools-tech.dwp_take: Adobe just gave Acrobat a serious workover, bolting on AI-powered search, content generation, and the ability to turn PDFs into interactive reports and podcasts. This matters because PDFs are still the cockroach of enterprise content, and if Adobe can actually make them useful in modern workflows instead of just being digital paper, people might stop cursing them. That said, I'll believe this works seamlessly when I see it actually deployed in the wild, because every "biggest update in years" promise eventually meets the reality of enterprise IT chaos.

tools-tech.title: No, AI is not killing jobs for everyone, studies say
tools-tech.excerpt: A slew of recent studies indicate that AI isn’t dramatically displacing workers. At the same time, there were no indicators that the fast-moving technology is creating a lot of jobs, even as AI skills
tools-tech.dwp_take: A bunch of new research suggests AI isn't actually causing mass layoffs across the board, though it's not exactly creating new jobs either, with the exception that AI skills themselves are weirdly hard to find. This matters because digital workplace leaders need to stop panicking about robots taking over and start focusing on actual workforce planning and upskilling programs instead of just throwing money at ChatGPT licenses. The real story here is pretty boring but honest: AI is reshuffling the deck for junior workers while experienced people mostly keep their chairs, which means your job security depends less on the technology and more on whether you're willing to learn it.

digital-culture.title: Is it better to be a good follower or a bad leader?
digital-culture.excerpt: Although leadership is often portrayed as a glamorous career destination, being put in a position of power or responsibility is by no means an indicator of your ability to actually lead effectively. I
digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company is asking whether it's better to be competent in a supporting role than incompetent in charge, which is basically asking if we should stop promoting the wrong people into management. This matters because digital workplace leaders often get promoted for technical skills or tenure rather than actual leadership ability, then they proceed to tank morale and productivity while we all suffer through their poorly run collaboration platforms and change initiatives. My take after three decades: most workplace dysfunction traces back to someone who was great at their job getting promoted into management hell, which is why so many teams secretly run themselves while their boss attends meetings.

digital-culture.title: 12 signs you’re becoming irrelevant at work (and what to do about it)
digital-culture.excerpt: Feeling overlooked in meetings or left out of key decisions can signal a troubling shift in your workplace standing. This article outlines 12 specific warning signs that your professional relevance ma
digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company published a piece about recognizing signs of professional irrelevance at work, like being excluded from meetings or decisions, plus strategies to fix it. For digital workplace folks, this matters because relevance in hybrid and distributed environments is harder to maintain when you're not physically visible, and visibility metrics have fundamentally changed. The irony is that most people feeling irrelevant are probably overthinking it while their colleagues are too busy drowning in Slack to notice anyone's relevance level anyway.

digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company named nine international companies as best workplaces for innovators in 2026, with seven also making the broader top 100 list, recognizing their investment in human capital and innovation infrastructure. For digital workplace pros, this matters because it shows that workplace tech and culture strategies travel across geographies, proving innovation isn't just a Silicon Valley thing anymore. The real story here is that most of these winners probably aren't obsessing over the latest AI chatbot, they're just nailing the basics: trust, autonomy, and actually listening to their people.

digital-culture.title: Best Workplaces for Innovators 2026: North America category winners

digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company just crowned 22 North American companies as best workplaces for innovators, ranging from tiny startups to established brands like Radio Flyer and Bose. For digital workplace folks, these lists matter because they signal what forward-thinking organizations are actually doing right operationally, even if the criteria remain fuzzy. My take: if your company's chasing innovation but still stuck in annual performance reviews and email-only communication, you're not fooling anybody, and Fast Company's judges probably wouldn't pick you either.

Honestly, the real story here is that Apple's predictable annual refresh cycle gives us a perfect excuse to finally update those five-year-old MacBook Airs gathering dust in the supply closet.

industry-news.title: Think 5,000mAh Is Big? These 10 Smartphones Go Much Higher
industry-news.excerpt: Compare 10 smartphones with batteries from 5,088mAh to 10,000mAh, plus gaming-test results that show why capacity alone cannot predict endurance. The post Think 5,000mAh Is Big? These 10 Smartphones G
industry-news.dwp_take: TechRepublic compared ten smartphones with massive batteries ranging from 5,088mAh to 10,000mAh and found that raw battery capacity doesn't actually predict real-world usage time. This matters because workplace professionals who manage device fleets or advise on employee smartphone choices need to understand that specs on paper don't equal all-day productivity without meetings killing your screen time. The real takeaway is that your CEO's shiny new phone with a 10,000mAh battery will still die by 3 p.m. if he's streaming video between back-to-back Zoom calls.

industry-news.dwp_take: Apple just dropped the iPhone 18 Pro with a new camera, faster processor, smarter Siri, and better battery life for twelve hundred bucks. industry-news.title: DealHub MCP Brings Agentic Control to Quote-to-Revenue
industry-news.excerpt: DealHub AI is extending agentic automation to the administration of quote-to-revenue systems. Its new MCP for Admin is designed to help teams update pricing rules, approval workflows, guided selling f
industry-news.dwp_take: DealHub has released an MCP for Admin that lets AI agents handle the configuration side of quote-to-revenue systems, managing things like pricing rules and approval workflows without stepping outside governance boundaries. For digital workplace teams, this matters because it means fewer manual admin tasks clogging up your sales ops people's calendars, which frees them to actually think instead of just clicking buttons all day. The real question is whether your governance structure is tight enough to trust an agent with these keys, because nothing says "fun Friday" like an AI quietly rewriting your approval workflows.
